slides.title: Custom Deleters with Smart Pointers
slides.prompt: Smart pointers can manage non-memory resources (like C file handles, sockets, database connections, or custom C-API pointers) by supplying custom deleter functions or lambdas instead of calling standard delete.

slides.title: decltype for Lambda Deleter
slides.prompt: Fill in the specifier used to pass a lambda type as a custom deleter template argument to std::unique_ptr.
slides.codeSnippet:
auto deleter = [](int* p){ delete p; };
std::unique_ptr<int, ___ (deleter)> ptr(new int(5), deleter);

slides.title: shared_ptr vs unique_ptr Deleter Type
slides.prompt: How do custom deleters differ between std::unique_ptr and std::shared_ptr in C++?
options: std::unique_ptr includes the deleter type in its template signature; std::shared_ptr erases the deleter type in its control block
std::shared_ptr requires template parameter for deleter; unique_ptr does not
std::unique_ptr supports lambdas; shared_ptr supports function pointers only
There is no difference in type specifications
slides.correctAnswer: std::unique_ptr includes the deleter type in its template signature; std::shared_ptr erases the deleter type in its control block

slides.title: Type Erasure in std::shared_ptr
slides.prompt: What is the benefit of type erasure for deleters in std::shared_ptr?
options: Containers like std::vector<std::shared_ptr<T>> can hold pointers with different custom deleters seamlessly
Eliminates heap allocation for control blocks
Allows shared_ptr to be passed without memory overhead
Speeds up destructor performance by making it non-virtual
slides.correctAnswer: Containers like std::vector<std::shared_ptr<T>> can hold pointers with different custom deleters seamlessly

slides.title: make_shared with Custom Deleter
slides.prompt: Can you pass a custom deleter directly as an argument to std::make_shared?
options: No, std::allocate_shared must be used instead when custom memory allocation or deleters are required
Yes, pass deleter as the first parameter to std::make_shared
Yes, pass deleter as the last parameter to std::make_shared
No, custom deleters are never supported with shared_ptr
slides.correctAnswer: No, std::allocate_shared must be used instead when custom memory allocation or deleters are required
